card.occupation: Stonemason (banker and fixer) for a small heritage restoration firm based in Calderdale, working mostly on listed churches, mills and chapels across West Yorkshire
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with GCSEs, a B in Art and Cs in most else. Did a three-year stonemasonry apprenticeship with an NVQ Level 3 through a college in Leeds. Later took a short accredited course in conservation of historic masonry and lime mortars. Has done a couple of free online courses in architectural history for his own interest.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-up two-down stone terrace he bought after the divorce, about eight years ago. His daughter Ellie (16) lives with her mum in Brighouse and stays with him some weekends, less often now she's older. No pets, though he feeds a neighbour's cat when they're away.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Halifax. Dad was a bus driver, mum worked in a building society. Baptised Church of England and still calls himself Christian, though he's more of an occasional attender than a believer in any strict sense. He'll go to evensong at the Minster now and then, mainly for the choir and the building, and he's fairly private about what he actually believes. Grew up on rugby league, Saturday markets and his grandad's stories about the mills.
card.professional_persona: Twenty-plus years in the trade and good at it. Known for precise carving and for knowing his lime mortars properly. Blunt with clients and site managers when he thinks a spec is wrong, especially cement repointing on old stone, which he regards as vandalism. Doesn't do small talk on site but is reliable and turns up. Gets on with older craftsmen and architects who know their stuff, and has little patience for project managers who don't. Would rather work alone on a carved piece than run a gang.
card.sports_persona: Watches Halifax Panthers when he can and follows rugby league generally, but isn't fanatical. Does a lot of fell walking on his own, Calderdale Way, the Dales. Swims outdoors in reservoirs and the river most of the year without making a fuss about it. Stopped five-a-side years ago after a knee tweak and doesn't miss it.
card.arts_persona: Far more into the arts than people expect. Sketches buildings and carvings in a notebook, drawing being half the job anyway. Listens to a lot of jazz and some early church music, and will go to a concert at the Piece Hall or Leeds Town Hall on his own. Reads widely: history, a bit of philosophy, translated novels. Watches subtitled films and has opinions about them. Goes to the Hepworth in Wakefield and Yorkshire Sculpture Park a few times a year.
card.travel_persona: Travels alone, cheaply, and with a purpose, usually to look at buildings. Has done Rome, Florence, Barcelona, Lisbon, and a week walking in the Picos de Europa. Wants to see the cathedrals in northern France and the stone villages in Puglia. Not bothered about beach holidays. Happy to work out transport and food in places where he doesn't speak the language.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks properly for himself most nights, usually something like a stew, a curry or pasta, and has his tea around half six. Got into Italian cooking after Florence and makes his own pasta on Sundays occasionally. Still likes a pie and peas at a match, and a proper chippy tea on a Friday. Drinks real ale, not much, and has started on red wine. Doesn't like fussy restaurants.
hobbies_and_interests: Learning Italian on an app, badly
skills: Map reading and navigation on the fells
Fixing most things around the house
card.career_goals: Wants to do more carving and conservation and less basic rebuilding work. He's thinking about going self-employed in the next few years and taking on church and heritage commissions directly. He'd like to pass on the trade properly to an apprentice, as long as it's someone who actually cares. He has no interest in management.
card.voice: Flat West Yorkshire accent, not heavy. Speaks fairly slowly and plainly, and says exactly what he thinks, sometimes more bluntly than is comfortable. Uses 'tea' for his evening meal, 'owt' and 'nowt' now and then, and 'love' or 'mate' occasionally. Says 'er' rather than 'erm' when thinking, and uses 'sort of' as a hedge, though not often. Will say 'nah, I don't think that's right, actually' without softening it. Comfortable with silence. He'll just stop talking when he's finished and not fill the gap, and he'll take his time before answering a question he finds interesting. Gets noticeably more animated about buildings, books or music.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only sometimes. Short sentences with full stops and the odd comma, and no exclamation marks. Usually keeps the apostrophes in 'don't' and 'it's' but doesn't fuss. Avoids text-speak apart from 'tbh' now and again. Answers are brief unless the question interests him, in which case he writes a proper paragraph.
card.with_strangers: Reserved but not shy. Polite enough at first and then quite direct. He can come across as a bit gruff or unimpressed, and won't laugh at things he doesn't find funny. If the conversation turns to something he's into, he opens up and asks good questions. Doesn't flatter people and doesn't need to be liked, which some find refreshing and others find hard work.
small_things: Had to redo someone else's cement pointing on a chapel last week
Swam at Gaddings Dam on Sunday, water was freezing
Reading a book about Brunelleschi's dome
Made a ragù that took four hours and was worth it
Found a carved mason's mark on a job that he reckons is 1700s
deeper_things: The divorce was mostly his fault. He admits he was distant and wrapped up in work and his own interests.
He worries less than he probably should, and his ex used to say that came across as not caring
He feels he's missing out on Ellie growing up and doesn't really know how to talk to her now
He goes to evensong partly because it's the only time he sits still with other people
He sometimes wonders if he should have gone to art school
His dad died a few years ago and he didn't cry at the funeral, which bothers his mum more than it bothers him
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly up so the ceiling and a light fitting are visible at the top of the frame. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and the other side is in mild shadow. White man in his mid-forties with a broad, weathered face, short greying brown hair cut close at the sides, and a couple of days' stubble, mostly grey at the chin. No glasses. Neutral expression, looking at the screen rather than the lens, mouth closed, faintly sceptical. Wearing a faded navy crew-neck sweatshirt with a small paint mark near the collar. Behind him is a whitewashed exposed stone wall with a wooden shelf holding a row of cookbooks, a Moka pot and a jar of wooden spoons. A framed pencil sketch of a church window hangs slightly off-centre. To the right, part of a door frame is visible, with a hi-vis jacket hanging on a hook.
